must_haves.note: AGENTS.md/PLAN.md confine work to continuityops/; forbid Project A/C edits.
Invoke-ContinuityOpsValidators.ps1 covers path_scope, secret_scan, independence_lock, partition_manifest, orchestration_model, project_a_untouched.
integration/upstreams.lock.json sets edits_project_a/c false and owns_lab_artifacts true.
README claim footer limits to synthetic lab; not customer-production SRE ownership.
STATUS.md marks Stage 2 complete while plan-approval.json status remains build-orchestration; accuracy-final.json candidate_sha lags HEAD.

findings.note: Authority metadata drift: STATUS/accuracy-final assert council completion at an older SHA while approval pin still says build-orchestration.
Validate entrypoint rewrites approval hashes on each run; operators must treat pins as mutable build tooling, not immutable certification.

strengths: Clear ContinuityOps-only authority and Ralphy stage model.
Allowlisted validators with independence and secret scans.
Orchestration policy, schemas, tasks, and handoffs present under harness/.

must_haves.note: network, eks, serverless, observability modules with versions/variables/outputs.
staging and recovery-lab compositions wire all four modules; recovery-lab documents synthetic/destructive purpose.
Bootstrap uses gated create flag, versioning, SSE, public-access block; no credentials in-repo.
CI workflow is explicitly draft with REPLACE_ME OIDC role; plan-only posture documented.
release-contract.json image_digest remains sha256:PENDING_BUILD; no built lab image pin yet.

findings.note: Lab image and OIDC account placeholders block live apply; compositions are offline-validate scaffolds.
No terraform test/validate harness artifacts under this partition beyond README offline commands.
EKS module is functional but minimal (public endpoint enabled; limited cluster hardening beyond private subnets for nodes).

strengths: Coherent module + environment layout with ContinuityOps tagging.
Serverless TF includes SQS+DLQ+Lambda IAM; observability includes log group and baseline alarm.
App contract documents smoke endpoints and separates lab from Project C releases.

must_haves.note: values.yaml sets digest pin, runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, drop ALL, HPA, PDB, NetworkPolicy egress allowlist.
Kyverno examples: require-digest, require-nonroot, deny-latest-tag.
Inject/restore scripts and docs for crashloop, DNS, networkpolicy, readiness, resource-pressure.
Test-ContinuityOpsChart.ps1 asserts required templates/keys and rejects AKIA patterns in values.
secret.create false; references external Secret name only.

findings.note: Chart test is structural/string-based; does not require helm template/lint when Helm is available.
Image digest PENDING_BUILD means chart cannot deploy as-is without operator fill-in.

strengths: Deployment template covers probes, topology spread, security contexts, and config checksum.
NetworkPolicy template encodes DNS + egress allowlist cleanly.
Scenarios are runnable kubectl patches useful for lab drills.

must_haves.note: Worker implements content-addressed keys, poison detection, structured logs, partial batch failures.
node:test suites for idempotency and parse present and aligned to contract.
idempotency.js documents in-memory lab store vs DynamoDB production recommendation.
sqs-dlq.md and worker.contract.json cover visibility timeout, DLQ, replay features.
serverless/infra is markdown scaffolding; deployable template remains TF module elsewhere, not a first-class SAM/CFN under this tree.

findings.note: In-memory idempotency/poison registries reset per cold start; fine for lab honesty but not multi-instance correctness.
worker.zip binary present; prefer reproducible build docs over opaque zip as sole artifact.

strengths: Readable handler with visibility/concurrency guidance comments.
Contract enumerates event types, logging fields, and test paths.
saas-lifecycle decision links async path to portfolio narrative.

must_haves.note: alerts.yaml entries include owner, SEV, runbook, dedupe, condition, recovery_condition.
slo-catalog.json defines availability/latency/worker SLOs with burn-rate and recovery targets.
collector-config.yaml deletes/hashes sensitive attributes; exporter tokens via env placeholders.
Test-AlertSchema.ps1 validates required fields, SEV range, dedupe, recovery.
service/kubernetes/serverless Grafana JSON dashboards present with RED-oriented panels.

findings.note: Catalogs are repo-only; not bound to live CloudWatch/Prometheus series or measured burn rates.
Some alert runbook links point at generic README/slo JSON rather than a pressure-specific runbook.

strengths: Burn-rate alert design maps cleanly to SRE multi-window practice.
Cross-links to k8s scenarios and serverless DLQ docs.
Secrets discipline in OTel headers/endpoints.

must_haves.note: Eight drill markdowns including misleading-latency and observability blind-spot.
Runbooks include do-not-yet / stop-escalation style guidance before mutation.
incidents/TEMPLATE.md and postmortems/TEMPLATE.md present.
operations README forbids live credentials/ARNs/tenant data in the tree.
Commands, timelines, hypothesis/ruled-out structure usable for tabletop or lab inject.

findings.note: No automated drill executor; usefulness depends on operator running kubectl/helm manually.
Change records live partly under P_resilience; ops partition focuses drills/runbooks (acceptable split).

strengths: Misleading-symptom drills teach diagnosis discipline, not just happy-path recovery.
kubectl-first-five is a strong triage entrypoint.
Clear mapping from drills to kubernetes scenarios and severity ownership.

must_haves.note: mutation-policy.json default_write false; mutation jobs require human approval and evidence.
Test-UnsafeProposals.ps1 + unsafe-proposal-cases.json cover injection, forged evidence, secrets, unauthorized mutation.
docs/guardrails/secrets.md bans plaintext secrets in git/chat; points to SM/SSM/OIDC.
EN/zh-CN incident-triage prompts document evidence→proposal without default mutation.
iam-rbac.md and supply-chain.md present under docs/guardrails.

findings.note: Unsafe-proposal tests are keyword/rule-id based, not an integration with a real agent runtime.
IAM depth is documentary plus module roles; no ContinuityOps-specific least-privilege review artifact beyond docs.

strengths: Product-control vs build-posture distinction is explicit and honest.
Negative cases are concrete and recruiter-demonstrable.
Secrets and mutation denial lists are operationally clear.

must_haves.note: rto-rpo.md tables components, methods, and lab aggregate tiers.
CH-backup-restore and CH-teardown procedures with synthetic-data preconditions.
restore-verification.schema.json requires synthetic_data_label and measured RTO/RPO fields.
finops.md labels dollar figures as synthetic estimates; budget/idle guidance present.
S7 evidence events table is stub; no populated restore-verification JSON bound to this candidate SHA.

findings.note: Performance baseline-results.json is explicitly illustrative/synthetic with zero SHA; must not be cited as measured lab proof.
Recovery capability is procedure+schema complete but not evidenced by a completed drill artifact.

strengths: Honest labeling of synthetic load and cost numbers.
Strong linkage from RTO targets to verification schema fields.
Teardown/retention thinking improves lab FinOps hygiene.

must_haves.note: claims-boundary.md lists supported vs not-claimed items including synthetic load honesty.
overview.md + flow.mmd cover control plane, runtime, operate loop, environments.
evidence/INDEX.md maps slices to artifacts with claim footer.
interview-walkthrough.md gives a six-step demo path ending on claims boundary.
Explicitly does not claim live customer-production apply or 24/7 SRE ownership.

findings.note: Portfolio partition is documentation-thin relative to runtime partitions; quality rests on cross-links.
Architecture still narrates Stage 2 accuracy loop process language; portfolio readers may confuse process meta with runtime proof.

strengths: Claims boundary is the right recruiter safety rail.
Evidence index and walkthrough make the tree demonstrable.
Language/severity decision docs support consistent ops narrative.

rationale: Across partitions this is a coherent, isolation-respecting ContinuityOps lab: real Terraform/Helm/worker code, validators and negative safety tests, strong drills/runbooks, and consistently honest synthetic/PENDING/draft labels. Residual gaps (PENDING image digest, draft OIDC, stub restore evidence, illustrative perf numbers, authority status/approval drift) reduce polish but are largely disclosed and do not undermine merge as a lab-grade portfolio scaffold.
